title: If You Hang a Box From a Rope...
sources: ASME, 'Elisha Graves Otis': in 1854 at the New York Crystal Palace exhibition Otis rode his platform up and had the rope cut; the safety (a wagon spring that engages ratchet teeth on the guide rails when the rope goes slack) stopped it
Guinness World Records, 'First safety elevator (lift)' / American Heritage, 'All safe, gentlemen, all safe!': the 1854 Crystal Palace demonstration in New York
HowStuffWorks, 'How Elevators Work: The Cable System': the counterweight weighs about as much as the car filled to about 40 percent of capacity, so the motor only has to overcome the difference
Wikipedia, 'Counterweight' / TK Elevator Classroom 'Counterweights': counterweight = car weight plus roughly 40-50 percent of rated load

HowStuffWorks, 'How Elevators Work: Safety Systems' / TK Elevator Classroom 'Governor module' / Otis 'High-rise safety systems': an overspeed governor's flyweights swing out when it spins too fast, the governor rope then trips the safeties, which wedge against the guide rails and stop the car
HowStuffWorks 'Safety Systems' / Science ABC 'How safe are you in an elevator': cars hang from several steel hoist ropes (often four to eight), so one breaking does not drop the car

lines.text: If you hang a box from a rope, you get an elevator.
lines.caps: If you hang a box | from a rope, | you get an elevator.

lines.text: But if that rope ever snaps, the box falls.
lines.caps: But if that rope | ever snaps, | the box falls.

lines.text: So, in eighteen fifty-four, Elisha Otis stood on a platform in New York, and had the rope cut.
lines.caps: So, in 1854, Elisha Otis | stood on a platform | in New York, | and had the rope cut.

lines.text: A spring snapped out, caught the teeth on the rails, and he didn't fall.
lines.caps: A spring snapped out, | caught the teeth | on the rails, | and he didn't fall.

lines.text: But pulling a heavy car up a tall building takes a huge motor.
lines.caps: But pulling a heavy car | up a tall building | takes a huge motor.

lines.text: So, a counterweight rides down while the car goes up,
lines.caps: So, a counterweight | rides down | while the car goes up,

lines.text: weighing as much as the car plus about forty percent of its load,
lines.caps: weighing as much as the car | plus about 40% | of its load,

lines.text: so the motor only lifts the difference.
lines.caps: so the motor | only lifts the difference.

lines.text: But what if the car starts moving way too fast?
lines.caps: But what if the car | starts moving | way too fast?

lines.text: So, a spinning governor up top keeps watch,
lines.caps: So, a spinning governor | up top keeps watch,

lines.text: and if it spins too fast, its weights fly out and trip steel wedges that clamp the rails.
lines.caps: and if it spins too fast, | its weights fly out | and trip steel wedges | that clamp the rails.

lines.text: And the car doesn't hang from one rope, but from several.
lines.caps: And the car doesn't hang | from one rope, | but from several.

lines.text: You see, the ropes just lift the car. The rails are what catch it.
lines.caps: You see, the ropes | just lift the car. | The rails | are what catch it.

lines.text: That's why every elevator you ride runs on two steel rails you never see.
lines.caps: That's why every elevator | you ride runs on | two steel rails | you never see.
